transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jamal (Triton Head of ML), Priya (Triton Platform), Noah (CTO, observer)
Shared items: slide deck (link: tiny.redwood/deck), benchmark sheet (link: tiny.redwood/bench), access checklist (link: tiny.redwood/access)

Summary:
High-level kickoff for the POC: agree success criteria, finalize workload sizing and benchmark gates, access plan, mid-point review cadence, and exec readout expectations. Decision path: pass/fail gates at mid-point and final exec readout. Primary risk: access timing and dataset anonymization.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency, throughput, quality thresholds)
- Benchmark workload (sample size, QPS, sequence lengths)
- Timeline (kickoff, access setup, mid-point, exec readout)
- Roles and access (S3, VPC peering, KMS)
- Decision points and fallbacks (hosted vs dedicated)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we can start, is that good on your side?
[00:07] Jamal: Yeah, we're good. Morning, afternoon — depends where you are. Thanks for doing this.
[00:11] Maya: Quick intros, real quick — I'm Maya, AE on the account, will coordinate runbook and timeline. Liam's our systems engineer who will own the benchmark harness.
[00:20] Liam: Hi all. I'll be leading perf tests, synthetic load, quickly explain the harness later.
[00:26] Priya: Priya, platform at Triton, I'll be setting up the test infra and access.
[00:29] Noah: Noah, CTO, just listening in for executive priorities.
[00:33] Jamal: And Jamal, Head of ML, driving model evaluation and success criteria.
[00:38] Maya: Cool. High level agenda: align on what 'success' looks like, define workload, access plan, mid-point checkpoint and exec readout. If we can land on who owns what today, we can start next week.
[00:48] Jamal: Sounds good. To set context: Triton runs a retrieval-augmented generation flow for our docs assistant. Typical throughput right now is about 120 qps during peak across shards, average seq len around 850 tokens after context, and we care about p95 latency under 600ms for user-facing requests. Cost is also an important metric.
[01:10] Liam: Okay that's helpful. Just to clarify, 120 qps is aggregate across the fleet or per endpoint?
[01:15] Jamal: Aggregate, across the public API cluster. For the POC we're going to isolate a single critical route so we can stress it.
[01:22] Maya: For the POC gating, how does Triton want to define pass/fail? Jamal, are you thinking strictly latency plus quality?
[01:31] Jamal: It's multi-dimensional — quality first (we need <10% delta on our NDCG rerank metrics compared to current baseline), latency p95 under 600ms, and throughput sustain for a 10 minute window at 80 qps. Also cost per 1M tokens should be within our target band, otherwise exec will be concerned.
[01:48] Priya: And from infra we'll require SOC2-ish compliance checks — we need audit logs and KMS integration; data residency: test data will be US-only.
[01:56] Maya: Noted. We'll include SOC2 checklist and show how Redwood Private supports KMS and audit logs. The default for the POC is our hosted sandbox but we can do Dedicated if needed.
[02:07] Liam: Quick note — when we talk about costs, quantization and batching will affect latency/cost trade-offs; we'll include a quantization profile matrix in the benchmark sheet.
[02:18] Jamal: Good. Can you walk through the proposed milestone sequence? Kickoff to exec readout, what are the exact gates?
[02:25] Maya: Yes. Proposed milestones: 1) Kickoff and access (week 0), 2) Baseline ingest and smoke tests (week 1), 3) Benchmark run and tuning (weeks 2-3), 4) Mid-point review (end of week 3) — decision gate, 5) Final runs and exec readout prep (week 4), 6) Exec readout (week 5).
[02:43] Priya: That seems tight but doable. We need at least one week for internal security review for granting roles.
[02:49] Maya: Understood. We can shift the mid-point to end of week 4 if the access provisioning slips, but we want a short runway to get meaningful perf runs.
[02:58] Jamal: What's the typical time for Redwood to provision the test environment and get S3 access?
[03:03] Liam: If we get the role and an S3 prefix, we can spin up a test instance and run smoke tests within 48 hours. VPC peering or private deployment takes longer — usually 5-7 business days.
[03:13] Priya: We'll aim to provide S3 read-only and an STS role by 2025-09-18. VPC will be a stretch for this POC.
[03:20] Maya: Perfect. That aligns with our template. We'll treat VPC as a blocker only if baseline tests require network-isolated data.
[03:27] Jamal: On datasets: we'll provide 20k sampled queries and 5k doc chunks for context testing. Liam, is that enough for a robust benchmark?
[03:36] Liam: That's a good start. For stable p95 numbers we like at least 10k interactive samples, but synthetic ramping will help for throughput tests. We'll combine real samples for quality metrics and synthetic traffic for load.
[03:45] Maya: On quality evaluation, Jamal asked for NDCG <10% delta. We'll import your evaluation harness. Jamal, any non-negotiables for evaluation scripts?
[03:54] Jamal: We need the same tokenization and prompt templates; if Redwood changes the prompt pipeline, numbers won't be comparable. So please confirm the exact model weights/variant and tokenizer.
[04:04] Liam: We'll mirror your pipeline — we'll run the model in the same sequence length and use the same tokenizer; small diffs sometimes happen due to model quantization, we will log them.
[04:12] Priya: Also we need logs for traceability — request IDs and trace IDs must map back to your traces.
[04:17] Maya: We can include per-request metadata and a mapping to your trace IDs in Redwood Console.
[04:22] Jamal: Great. Let's talk about benchmark metrics — what should we measure?
[04:27] Liam: We'll measure p50/p90/p95 latency, tail latency, throughput (qps sustained), tokens/sec, CPU/GPU util, memory, and cost breakdown per 1M tokens. We'll also capture model quality scores (NDCG, BLEU if applicable) per run.
[04:39] Maya: We'll add a column for 'operational flags' — e.g., batch size, kv-cache hit rate, quantization profile used.
[04:45] Jamal: For the throughput target, we want a sustained 80 qps with p95 < 600ms for the RAG route. If it can't meet that on hosted plan, what's the recommended next step? Dedicated?
[04:56] Liam: Usually move to Redwood Dedicated or heavier instance types; we'll recommend a capacity profile. We'll provide cost delta for Hosted vs Dedicated in the bench sheet.
[05:05] Maya: I'll include a decision tree in the runbook: if hosted can't meet throughput at target latency, move to Dedicated evaluation; if Dedicated still doesn't pass, consider model distillation or more aggressive quantization and re-evaluate quality impact.
[05:17] Noah: From an exec perspective I just want to see clear stop/go criteria and cost delta. Avoid surprises in the readout.
[05:23] Maya: Totally. We'll provide a one-slide summary for the exec readout with pass/fail and cost delta.
[05:27] Jamal: What about billing and usage visibility during the POC?
[05:30] Maya: Redwood Console's POC dashboard gives token-level cost breakdown, per-run latency distributions, and model variant comparisons. We'll give Triton access with RBAC limited to the POC project.
[05:40] Priya: We'll need audit logs to be stored for 90 days. Is that configurable?
[05:44] Liam: Yes, we can configure retention windows; for Private deployments retention can be longer. We'll note retention settings in the access checklist.
[05:52] Jamal: I want to call out that security will look at KMS integration if we bring any PII into the test corpus. For now it's synthetic anonymized, but keep the option open.
[06:01] Maya: Understood. We'll document KMS flow and how keys are customer-controlled with Redwood Private.
[06:07] Jamal: Ok, timeline: if we get S3 by 9/18 — how soon can you run the first baseline?
[06:12] Liam: Baseline smoke within 48-72 hours after access. Full benchmark runs during week 2 and 3. Mid-point at end of week 3 to review early runs and tune.
[06:20] Priya: If that slips due to security sign-off, can we push the mid-point a week?
[06:24] Maya: Yes, we can shift but we'll then condense final runs. We'll aim to keep a 5-week overall window to meet your exec timeline.
[06:31] Jamal: For mid-point review, who should attend from Triton? I want ML lead and platform lead, and maybe a PM.
[06:36] Jamal: So Jamal, Priya, and product PM Aria (Triton) — we'll invite Aria to the mid-point.
[06:41] Maya: Great. On the exec readout — who will present from Triton?
[06:45] Noah: I will present, Jamal will do the technical voice.
[06:48] Jamal: Fine with that.
[06:50] Liam: A technical detail: for throughput runs we recommend a synthetic generator that maintains KV cache state realism; if we don't emulate KV cache hits we can get artificially higher latency.
[07:00] Maya: We'll capture that in the runbook: synthetic load should include warm/fill runs to populate KV caches before measurement windows.
[07:07] Priya: About data sandboxing — we'll give a test prefix on S3 with sanitized docs and a small set of user queries. Any special IAM needs?
[07:15] Liam: Read-only S3 plus an assume-role with STS for limited timeframe is fine. For observability, a write-only logging endpoint to your Splunk/Datadog would be nice but not required.
[07:24] Priya: We'll enable a CloudWatch subscription that streams logs to your endpoint; we'll follow the access checklist.
[07:29] Maya: I'll send the access checklist after the call.
[07:33] Jamal: Regarding quality gating — if we see >10% drop in NDCG with quantized model, is the plan to stop or to explore alternative quant profiles?
[07:41] Liam: We'll explore alternative quant profiles; we'll try 4-bit/8-bit mixes and a middle ground. If quality can't be recovered we mark it as a failed gate and present options at mid-point.
[07:50] Maya: Ok, decision path point: mid-point has three outcomes — green: continue to final runs; amber: continue but requires Dedicated evaluation or model tweaks; red: stop and produce findings for exec. We'll document this in the runbook.
[08:03] Jamal: That sounds good. On success criteria ownership — Jamal will sign off on quality, Priya on infra, Maya on Redwood deliverables. Noah signs exec readout acceptance.
[08:12] Maya: I'll add that RACI to the runbook.
[08:15] Jamal: Any concerns about model versioning? We want the pinned model to be exactly reproducible.
[08:20] Liam: We'll pin a Git SHA for the model config and model artifact version; Redwood Console captures model version metadata. Slight transcription note: sometimes model variant names in our console get shorted, so we'll include explicit hashes.
[08:33] Priya: For benchmark runs, what about cold-start vs warm-start distinctions? We want both measured.
[08:38] Liam: Yes we'll run cold-starts (fresh server) and warm-starts (after 10 minutes of warm traffic), and we'll separate those in the results.
[08:45] Jamal: Anything else for gating? What about error rates and stability?
[08:49] Maya: We'll include error rate threshold (5xx < 0.1%) and stability — no more than 3 restarts in a 24-hour window during the runs.
[08:58] Priya: Good. About the reporting cadence: weekly syncs and a 30-minute mid-point deep-dive?
[09:03] Maya: Yes weekly 30-minute check-ins; mid-point we'll do an hour deep-dive. Proposed weekly time: Tue 14:00 US/Eastern.
[09:11] Jamal: Works for us.
[09:13] Maya: Okay, imaging the bench sheet you'll get: tab for run configs, tab for results, tab for cost breakdown, and a decision tree. We'll attach an example run AND a script.
[09:24] Maya: I'm going to call out the order of operations we'll commit to: 1) Access, 2) Smoke baseline, 3) Quality eval on 10k samples, 4) Throughput and latency runs, 5) Tuning, 6) Mid-point review.
[09:37] Jamal: Makes sense. A small ask — can Redwood provide a quick handwritten runbook for our security team that explains KMS and data flows? Security tends to accept docs easier than slides.
[09:46] Maya: Yes, we'll provide a 1-page security runbook and the SOC2 docs.
[09:50] Priya: Also we need an NDA addendum for the POC environment — legal will send you a boilerplate.
[09:55] Maya: Great, we'll review.
[09:58] Jamal: Anything else on the technical side?
[10:01] Liam: One more: we'll include a synthetic replay tool to emulate user session patterns; that will help with KV-cache realism. We'll hand over the script in our first deliverable.
[10:11] Maya: Cool. Let's surface the explicit next steps for clarity.
[10:14] Maya: Next steps (high level): Redwood shares benchmark matrix + runbook by 9/15; Triton provides S3 prefix and STS role by 9/18; Redwood completes smoke baseline within 72 hours of access; schedule mid-point for week of 10/2.
[10:28] Jamal: I'll get stakeholder list and success criteria doc to you by 9/14.
[10:32] Priya: We'll start on IAM today and target the 9/18 date.
[10:36] Maya: Perfect. Any final questions?
[10:39] Noah: No, just make sure the exec deck is concise.
[10:42] Maya: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll send the runbook and bench sheet after this call.
[10:48] Jamal: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on imperfect transcription: some product names transcribed as 'Redwood dedicate' or 'KV cash'. Natural disfluencies present.

References shared during call:
- Benchmark sheet: tiny.redwood/bench
- Access checklist: tiny.redwood/access
- Security runbook (to be sent): note in next steps

Decision log (informal):
- Mid-point gate defined: green/amber/red with corresponding actions (continue, evaluate Dedicated, stop and brief exec)
- Primary success criteria: NDCG delta <10%, p95 <600ms, sustain 80 qps for 10m window, cost per 1M tokens within target band
